# Your money is still yours. We’re working to get it moving again.

**Tuesday, 10 November 2026**  
*By Inês, Product Designer at Pinha*

If you’ve tried to withdraw money from Pinha since Friday, you’ve found that you can’t. We should have told you sooner and more clearly what happened. I’m sorry.

On 6 November, our payments partner, Northvale Payments, blocked all outgoing transfers from its accounts without warning. Deposits and round-ups stopped too. That meant you couldn’t move your money, even though it’s yours and even though Northvale had given us notice that our relationship would end in 30 days.

We’re angry about what Northvale did. We’re also angry with ourselves for relying on a single partner without a backup. You deserve to hear both things plainly.

## What happened

Northvale, an electronic money institution based in Vilnius, holds Pinha customers’ money in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own funds. On 4 November, Northvale emailed us to say it was terminating its commercial relationship with Pinha, giving 30 days’ notice and citing a “risk appetite review.”

Two days later, at 09:00 on 6 November, it blocked outgoing transfers. Deposits and round-ups were stopped as well. That was not the orderly 30-day wind-down we had been told to expect.

We have tried to reach Northvale for answers. Its account manager stopped answering our calls on Friday, and its phone line now goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian. We don’t yet have a full explanation for why it acted this way. We won’t pretend otherwise.

## What we know about your money

Your money has not disappeared. It is held in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own money, and Northvale cannot use it for its own purposes.

But safeguarding doesn’t mean we can move it whenever we want. Right now, we cannot transfer your balance while Northvale is blocking outgoing payments. We need Northvale to release the funds and send us the balances file needed to move customer accounts. We’re pursuing that now.

We’ve signed a new partnership with Ostra Bank in Lisbon. To migrate accounts, we need Northvale to provide that balances file and we need Banco de Portugal’s approval. Our current estimate is **10 to 15 working days** for the process. That is an estimate, not a promise or a date we can guarantee. We’ll update you as we learn more.

On 7 November, we filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and the Bank of Lithuania. We’re continuing to work with the relevant authorities and to press Northvale to release the funds and provide what’s needed for the migration.

## If you need money urgently

If you have an urgent need — for example, rent, medical costs or a job-related emergency — email **urgent@pinha.example** with **URGENTE** in the subject line. Please explain what you need and why, and include any relevant deadline. We’re trying to arrange individual releases for urgent cases. We can’t promise that Northvale will approve or process one, but we will review your message and do what we can.

Since Friday, we’ve received around 1,900 support emails. Our support team is three people, and replies are taking about two days at the moment. We’re sorry you’re having to wait. If you’ve already written to us, please don’t send the same message again unless something has changed or your situation has become urgent; that helps the team get through everyone’s messages.

We’ve cancelled the Pinha monthly fee for November and December for everyone.

## We got this wrong

Pinha was built to help you save a little at a time. Our app says: “your money is always yours, take it out anytime.” I designed that screen. I believed in those words, and I can understand why they feel hollow right now.

We trusted one payments partner and didn’t have a backup ready. That was our mistake. You have every right to be angry with Northvale, and with us. We won’t tell you to calm down, and we won’t ask you to be patient as if this were a minor inconvenience. We know this is your money, and that being unable to reach it can affect real plans and real bills.

We heard from someone in Porto who had saved for three years toward a car deposit. The seller is holding the car until Friday, 13 November. I read her message on the metro and nearly cried. I can’t promise we’ll solve her case in time. I can say we’re trying to help her, and that we understand this isn’t an abstract balance on a screen.

## What happens next

We’ll post updates here every **Monday and Thursday** until this is resolved, even if there’s no major change to report. We’ll be clear about what has moved, what hasn’t, and what we’re waiting on. We won’t publish a date we can’t stand behind.

For now:

- Your money remains in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own funds.
- Withdrawals are blocked, and deposits and round-ups are paused.
- We need Northvale to release the funds and send the balances file; the migration to Ostra also needs Banco de Portugal’s approval.
- If your need is urgent, email **urgent@pinha.example** with **URGENTE** in the subject line.
- November and December monthly fees are cancelled for everyone.
- We’ll update this blog every Monday and Thursday.

I’m sorry we put you in this position. I’m sorry our app made a promise that our setup couldn’t protect when a partner failed us. We’re focused on getting your money moving again, and on being honest with you while we work to do that.

— Inês, Product Designer at Pinha
